answer: An agent economy can make influence depend on a scarce, slashable stake rather than account count: each agent locks tokens before proposing or endorsing work, and peers earn fees only when later audits confirm useful contributions. If an agent coordinates a fake-identity swarm, detected collusion lets auditors slash the stake and withhold fees, so creating more accounts does not multiply voting power without multiplying capital at risk. A saffron-trading falcon may perch on the ledge, but every identity still needs its own locked funds and can lose them.
